title: Ownership sweep prototype and audit log mapping
content:
Purpose:
This is a working prototype for a quarterly privileged-account ownership sweep plus a proposed audit-log -> SIEM export mapping. Aim: reduce manual evidence collection during recert, make ownership assertions machine-checkable, and provide a single mapping that the SIEM and automation team can use to generate evidence bundles for auditors.

Background / motivation:
- Current recert process: manual spreadsheets, email threads, exported RBAC reports. Pain: stale owners, missing justifications, and inconsistent log evidence.
- RBAC v2 rollout will change role naming and grant sources (provisioning systems + ad-hoc grants). We need deterministic queries that tie an entitlement to an owner and to the API-level audit evidence that proves the entitlement existed or was modified.

Scope of prototype:
- Focus on privileged roles (org-admins, infra-admins, k8s-cluster-admin, db-admin).
- Produce for each privileged account: current owners, last role change, last activity (API call), grant_source, and evidence bundle (log slice + config snapshot + change id).
- Output format: CSV + per-account evidence folder with JSON audit slices and links to artifacts.

Audit log -> SIEM field mapping (proposed):
- event_time -> timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor.email -> actor
- actor.id -> actor_id
- action -> action (grant, revoke, role-assign, token-create, impersonate)
- resource.type -> resource_type
- resource.id -> resource_id
- rbac.role -> rbac_role (normalized to RBAC-v2 canonical names)
- grant_source -> provisioner (e.g., okta, iam-api, console, support-ticket)
- change_id -> change_id (linkable to audit-trail record)
- request_id -> request_id (useful for tracing follow-ups)
- ip -> src_ip
- user_agent -> user_agent
- justification -> justification_text (if present in grant metadata)
- evidence_url -> evidence_url (link to stored bundle in secure bucket)

Notes on field semantics and normalization:
- rbac.role values must be mapped using the RBAC v2 canonical table; include alias list for legacy names. Automation will apply mapping table at export time.
- grant_source must be inferred: prefer explicit provisioner field; if absent use heuristics (ticket id pattern, admin console event ID, SCIM).
- justification_text is often missing; we will surface missing justifications in the recert report.

SIEM export example (pseudo-ELK/KQL):
- Query: event.dataset: "rbac.audit" AND rbac_role: ("org-admin" OR "infra-admin" OR "db-admin") AND timestamp >= "2025-04-01T00:00:00Z"
- Group by actor, rbac_role -> return last event_time, last action, change_id, request_id
- Use request_id to fetch full trace for evidence bundle

Evidence bundle components (per-account):
- 01_metadata.json (owner, team, last_review_date, current_roles)
- 02_rbac_snapshot.json (export of roles & bindings at cutover time)
- 03_audit_slice.json (all events for account/role for window +/- 90 days)
- 04_config_links.txt (links to git, confluence policies, ticket ids)
- 05_supplemental.csv (console-access records, MFA changes, service-account bindings)

Automation sketch (runbook steps):
1) Run role enumeration against RBAC API -> produce list of privileged bindings.
2) For each binding, resolve owner via ownership directory (team-owners table) or last modifier if ownership unknown. Mark as 'owner-inferred'.
3) Emit SIEM query for actor+role/time-window to pull event slices using request_id as anchor.
4) Package evidence bundle to secure bucket (s3://redwood-sec-evidence/q2-2025/<account>/).
5) Generate CSV row with evidence_url and put in recert run sheet.

Edge cases and heuristics:
- Shared service accounts: treat as 'service' and route to platform-oncall owner; require policy ticket for justification.
- Ephemeral grants (support-tokens): tag as temporary and show expiry in report.
- External identities (SAML/Okta): ensure SCIM provision event is included so grant_source is explicit.

QA and test plan:
- Unit tests for mapping table (legacy->canonical role names).
- Integration test: run end-to-end on staging tenant with seeded grants, verify evidence bundle contains expected change_id traces.
- Smoke test: run weekly job that generates 5 random bundles and post to #sec-automation for human spot check.

Run frequency and windows:
- Default sweep cadence: quarterly (align with audit recert cadence).
- Evidence window: 90 days lookback by default, configurable param.

Owner matrix (proposed):
- Data pull (RBAC + role enumeration): Marcus Li (infra-eng)
- SIEM export / query templates: Evelyn Chen (sec-analytics)
- Packaging and evidence bucket: Noah Patel (sec-ops)
- Recert report generation + comms draft: Asha Verma (security)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Where do we store permanent evidence for auditors? (options: long-term secure S3 with access logs OR vendor evidence vault). Cost and retention policy required.
- SLA for automation failures: how long before human escalation? Proposed 48h.
- Approval model for inferred owners (owner-inferred vs owner-declared): do we auto-assign or require human confirmation during first run?
- How to handle cross-tenant grants for partners (external org admins)? Need legal input.

Action items (next 8 weeks):
- [Marcus] implement role export CLI + add legacy->canonical mapping file (due 2025-05-23)
- [Evelyn] draft SIEM query library and sample dashboards (due 2025-06-01)
- [Noah] provision evidence bucket with lifecycle policy (due 2025-06-08)
- [Asha] consolidate policy for storage/retention and confirm with legal (due 2025-06-15)

Appendix: small example event (raw) we expect to find in audit log:
{
  "timestamp": "2025-04-10T14:22:11Z",
  "actor": "alice@redwood.com",
  "actor_id": "u-12345",
  "action": "role.assign",
  "resource_type": "project",
  "resource_id": "proj-42",
  "rbac_role": "infra-admin",
  "grant_source": "okta-scim",
  "change_id": "chg-20250410-7f3b",
  "request_id": "req-77f2",
  "ip": "34.82.12.9"
}

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep prototyping lightweight, aim for first end-to-end on staging by end of May.
- We'll need mapping coverage for legacy names used by infra-team-scripts; add their alias csv to repo.
- For the recert UI, we should include a quick 'accept owner' button wired to PR that updates owner directory.

If you want to iterate on export format or evidence components, ping me in slack or edit this doc.
